CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to evaluate the effectiveness of the current treatment plan for generalized anxiety disorder, insomnia, persistent fatigue, and tension-type headaches, and to address any new concerns that have arisen since the last visit.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his scheduled follow-up appointment, reporting a mixture of improvements and ongoing challenges. He states that his anxiety levels have remained stable since the last visit, but he continues to experience episodes of irritability and difficulty concentrating, particularly during high-stress periods at work. He has adhered to the prescribed sertraline dose of 300 mg daily but expresses frustration at the lack of significant mood stabilization.
His tension-type headaches have further decreased, now occurring approximately once a week, with an average intensity rating of 3 out of 10. Mr. Smith notes that the increased dosage of topiramate to 150 mg daily has been effective, and he has successfully minimized his ibuprofen usage to once a week, due to his ongoing concerns regarding gastrointestinal side effects.
Sleep quality has shown further improvement; Mr. Smith reports averaging 8 hours of sleep per night, though he still encounters difficulty falling asleep on particularly anxious nights. He continues to take trazodone at 75 mg at bedtime, which he finds effective, although he has experienced some residual drowsiness. Mr. Smith reports that he has discontinued gabapentin, as he felt the sedation was too pronounced and counterproductive.
Despite these positive changes, Mr. Smith continues to struggle with persistent fatigue, particularly in the afternoons, which he describes as debilitating at times. He has attempted to implement lifestyle modifications, including increased physical activity and mindfulness practices, but still finds his energy levels insufficient for daily tasks.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 300 mg daily (continued) 2. Trazodone 75 mg at bedtime (continued) 3. Melatonin 10 mg at bedtime (discontinued) 4. Lisinopril 10 mg daily (continued) 5. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief (continued) 6. Amitriptyline 50 mg nightly (continued) 7. Topiramate 150 mg daily (continued) 8. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (continued) 9. Gabapentin 200 mg at bedtime (discontinued)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith has maintained his commitment to physical activity, regularly participating in lunchtime walks and weekend hikes. He reports continued adherence to a balanced diet and has successfully reduced his caffeine intake. He has actively engaged in mindfulness techniques, including meditation and yoga, which he finds beneficial in managing his anxiety symptoms. He has also started journaling to track his mood and stress levels, which he believes has aided in his self-reflection.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Anxiety levels stable; mild irritability persists; sleep quality improved; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms. - Neurological: Headache frequency decreased; no dizziness or visual disturbances reported. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue noted, particularly in the afternoons, with no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 120/76 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert, oriented; appears well-rested; mood appears anxious but engaged. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed; no tenderness in the temporal region. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears anxious with mild distress.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 300 mg daily. Recommend referral for cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) to further address persistent irritability and concentration issues. 2. Insomnia: Continue trazodone at 75 mg at bedtime; reassess efficacy and side effects in one month. Discontinue melatonin due to lack of benefit. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue topiramate at 150 mg daily; monitor headache frequency and intensity with headache diary. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Encourage ongoing lifestyle modifications and consider a referral to a sleep specialist if fatigue persists. Evaluate for possible underlying conditions such as sleep apnea or thyroid dysfunction.
Follow-up appointment is scheduled for 2029-01-26 to evaluate symptom progression, medication efficacy, and discuss any new concerns. Mr. Smith is encouraged to maintain an open dialogue regarding his treatment response and any lifestyle changes he implements.
